scope: Native application-owned MariaDB capture and explicit recovery through the outside-host controller
verified: Actual application-owned mariadb-dump streams through pinned SSH into a bounded authenticated encrypted archive outside the application owner.
The controller and native owner independently hash the SQL stream; decrypted archive readback verifies every captured byte before the backup is accepted.
Native capture checks the actual holds, database connections, event-writer state and complete original database fingerprint before and after the dump.
Recovery requires the existing durable native restore intent, original captured SQL identity, reviewed backup pair and fresh writer observations.
The full encrypted archive is authenticated before the application account empties its exact recovery target; SQL then streams directly to the native MariaDB client without a plaintext SQL file.
A corrupted archive, a foreign SQL hash and an attempt to empty the target without its durable intent are refused before database mutation.

An interrupted multi-frame SQL restore leaves the restore intent unresolved and web requests held; a separate explicit restore reproduces the original rows, schema, views, triggers and sequence counters.
Independent native fingerprint confirmation and original file/cache verification precede restoration of web routing and schedules.
Windows DPAPI archives remain bound to the current Windows user; the Linux fixture uses an explicit AES-256-GCM key unavailable to either native application owner.
limits: The production CLI still exposes inspection and early preparation cleanup only; transfer is an imported API requiring explicit native configurations and actual writer observations.
The live production writer observer and forward release coordinator remain to be connected and the full candidate rehearsed together.
Synthetic native fixtures do not establish a held production backup or authorize production cutover.
No production hold, data mutation, provider write, payroll execution or payment occurred.
